children: JPMorgan has downgraded sportswear giants Adidas (ADDYY) and Puma (PMMAF), warning of a tougher growth environment in 2027 as intensifying competition threatens to squeeze sales and profitability across the athletic footwear and apparel industry.
The development also carries implications for Nike
, which is working to regain market share in an increasingly competitive sportswear market.
JPMorgan analyst Chiara Battistini downgraded Adidas to Neutral from Overweight, slashing her price target by 20% to 184 from 230.

Meanwhile, analyst Wendy Liu downgraded Puma to Underweight from Neutral, lowering her price target to 21 from 26. One of the biggest concerns surrounding Adidas is whether the company can sustain its sales momentum following the 2026 FIFA World Cup.JPMorgan expects Adidas' apparel sales to grow 5% in 2027, considerably below Wall Street's consensus estimate of 9%.
Puma faces a different challenge. The bank believes retailers are becoming increasingly reluctant to allocate valuable shelf space to brands undergoing turnaround efforts.
JPMorgan also expects Puma's operating expenses to rise 1% in 2027, compared with consensus expectations for a 2% decline.
Interestingly, Swiss sportswear company On Holding
remains JPMorgan's preferred stock in the sector, highlighting the growing importance of brand-specific momentum in a slowing market.
For Nike, Adidas and Puma investors, the biggest question heading into 2027 is whether these companies can protect their profit margins without sacrificing market share.
Slower industry growth could force established brands to offer heavier discounts and spend more aggressively on marketing, potentially undermining profitability.
Investors should closely monitor inventory levels, wholesale orders, gross margins and full-price merchandise sales in upcoming earnings reports.
Nike's turnaround could also intensify competitive pressure on Adidas and Puma as the American sportswear giant looks to reclaim lost ground.
Ultimately, JPMorgan's downgrades suggest that gaining market share may become increasingly important as overall industry growth moderates.

title: JPMorgan Drops Stark Warning on Adidas, Puma Stocks
